extracted.intended_audience: non-profit organizations, community-based grant writers, and agency staff preparing funding proposals
extracted.subtask_description: Practical training materials and checklists for planning programs and preparing funder-ready grant proposals for nonprofit/community-based organizations, covering vision, program design, evaluation, budgets, fiscal controls, and submission logistics.

rubrics_metrics.name: Vision
rubrics_metrics.description: The Vision of a project talks about its heart. It clearly describes the value of the Project and lets us know why & what changes will happen because the Project is there.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Consumers/Participants should be able to completely see & understand how the project will work in their best interest. The vision describes why the project is being created and what changes will occur as a result.

rubrics_metrics.name: Program Design (Design)
rubrics_metrics.description: The Program Design explains the Vision and details the fine points of the project from its service delivery and methodology to naming potential community partners and associations.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The Design describes the program’s audience, strategic partners, objectives, and purpose, and should detail service delivery, methods, who conducts interventions, duration & frequency, recruitment, activities/tasks, sequence/timeline, and relation to the mission.

rubrics_metrics.name: Organizational Capacity
rubrics_metrics.description: Agencies are accountable for their programs; funders want to know that their investments are secure and that the organization can handle the task it has put before itself.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Demonstrate ability to deliver goals and objectives, show agency infrastructure, staff expertise, fiscal responsibility, history of service, capacity to manage grants, and procedures (e.g., payroll, time sheets, accounting).

rubrics_metrics.name: Planning Basics / Project Planning
rubrics_metrics.description: Start with your clients in mind: plan programs by focusing on client needs and define products/services required.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Narrow the target audience, develop & implement a needs assessment, analyze data, gain consumer support, position project services in the community, solicit collaborations/partnerships, assess agency ability to deliver, and prepare agency & community for delivery and sustainability.

rubrics_metrics.name: Programming Designs — New Programs
rubrics_metrics.description: New Programs: programs which are new and have been constructed to fill gap services.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Show clear, descriptive expertise; services that seek to fill gaps; direct relationship to the mission; solid links to consumers; consumer input to programming; strong agency fiscal responsibility; how safety concerns are addressed; community linkages; how you prepared consumers; relationships between direct & indirect services.

rubrics_metrics.name: Programming Designs — Existing Programs
rubrics_metrics.description: Existing Programs: programs that are currently running and are seeking to be expanded and/or sustained.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Highlight consumer trust and participation; describe list of services; highlight program efficacy; utilize consumer quotes in marketing strategy; discuss agency’s goals & objectives; share lessons learned; relate philosophies to constituency; market best practices and success; inform audience of agency history.

rubrics_metrics.name: Programming Designs — Collaborative Programs
rubrics_metrics.description: Collaborative Programs: shared programming between strategic partners.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Highlight consumer trust and participation; utilize consumer quotes in marketing; describe services; highlight collaborative efficacy; discuss collaborative goals & objectives; relate philosophies to practices; inform audience of collaborative history; share lessons learned and best practices.

rubrics_metrics.name: Programming Designs — Organizational Programs
rubrics_metrics.description: Organizational Programming: programs that are essential to the continued operations of an agency, organization or association.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use needs assessment to strengthen program functioning; implement consumer suggestions/feedback; provide staff development and training to increase program solvency; translate community & consumer interactions into programming strategy.

rubrics_metrics.name: Programming Designs — Systemic Change Programs
rubrics_metrics.description: Systemic Change Programs: programs meant to produce change within and/or educate communities or populations.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Define area/region and scope of services; provide toll-free/local numbers; work collaboratively; have and use a budget to develop messages with consumer targets; partner with private and public agencies; utilize a governing body throughout campaign; be inclusive to maximize message implementation; personalize statistics.

rubrics_metrics.name: What funders typically look for — Organizational Capacity
rubrics_metrics.description: Funders need to know that your agency is able to deliver the goals and objectives that your application says it will.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Demonstrate staffing, infrastructure, fiscal controls, history, and management systems showing capacity to implement and sustain proposed activities.

rubrics_metrics.name: What funders typically look for — Feasibility of Objectives & Workplan
rubrics_metrics.description: An agency must demonstrate it can create and sustain logical and reasonable programming; workplans should be clear, understandable and within agency’s ability to complete in the funding cycle.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Ensure timeline, tasks, staff capacity, and measurable objectives align with organizational capacity and funding period.

rubrics_metrics.name: What funders typically look for — Appropriateness of Activities & Intervention
rubrics_metrics.description: Activities/interventions must match the funder's interests and be appropriate for the target population and context.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Do homework on funders before applying; avoid applying to funders whose priorities don't match your project; demonstrate culturally relevant, evidence-informed interventions.

rubrics_metrics.name: What funders typically look for — Collaborative Efforts
rubrics_metrics.description: Collaborations demonstrate an agency’s proficiency and ability to successfully work in their selected field of service in a targeted community.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Show peer organization support and strategic partnerships (on paper and in practice), describe partner roles, scope of collaboration, and shared history.

rubrics_metrics.name: What funders typically look for — Evaluation Methods
rubrics_metrics.description: Funders expect a plan for evaluating programming; evaluation shows whether a program is successful and how results will be used.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Establish evaluation questions, data types, collection methods, success criteria, whether to hire outside evaluator, and plans to use and disseminate results.

rubrics_metrics.name: RFP Typical Components (cover letter, abstract, narrative, mission, org summary, program description, evaluation, budget, attachments)
rubrics_metrics.description: Typical RFP components include: Cover Letter; Abstract; Program Narrative; Mission Statement; Organizational Summary; Program Description; Evaluation Methodology; Budgetary Process; Attachments.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Each component must be prepared carefully and align with funder instructions; see individual component entries for details.

rubrics_metrics.name: Cover Letter (RFP component)
rubrics_metrics.description: Cover Letter: your introduction to the funder. State support of the program from your board of directors & target audience; provide initial impression of your agency and target audience.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Include a one-sentence description of program purpose, audience, funding request, time frame & contact information; be focused, direct, and brief.

rubrics_metrics.name: Abstract (RFP component)
rubrics_metrics.description: Abstract describes your application to the funder: agency name, project title, target audience, project description including agencies involved, target population, goals & objectives, and outlines the budget & narrative.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Usually written last; concise summary of application for reviewer quick-read.

rubrics_metrics.name: Program Narrative (Design) (RFP component)
rubrics_metrics.description: Program Narrative defines the service delivery to clients, establishes contact frequency, outlines theory base, highlights who will conduct interventions, covers duration & frequency, and describes initiation.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Include partners/collaborators, recruitment strategy, activities/tasks in the workplan, sequences/timeline, and relate program to mission; use action words (e.g., Increase HIV knowledge; Decrease unintended pregnancies).

rubrics_metrics.name: Mission Statement (Vision) (RFP component)
rubrics_metrics.description: Mission Statement is the heart, goal and vision of your agency; it defines why & how you operate.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Draft should answer: What services does agency provide? Who benefits? What does the organization want to change? Combine elements into concise mission (example provided).

rubrics_metrics.name: Organizational Summary (Capacity) (RFP component)
rubrics_metrics.description: Organizational Summary includes who you serve (target population) and your history of service to the community.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use to demonstrate credibility, reach, and prior outcomes relevant to proposed project.

rubrics_metrics.name: Program Description (Design) (RFP component)
rubrics_metrics.description: Program Description should include partner backgrounds, scope of collaboration, time frame, staff & volunteers, budget, and management of the grant/funding request.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Work plans, tasks, timelines should mirror goals and objectives; be specific about roles and resources.

rubrics_metrics.name: GOAM — Suggested Evaluation Process
rubrics_metrics.description: GOAM: Goals (what program is meant to produce), Objectives (tasks to complete goals), Activities (specific tasks taken to accomplish objectives), Milestones (significant points occurring as goals are accomplished).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use GOAM structure to link evaluation metrics to program operations and to define measurable steps toward goals.

rubrics_metrics.name: SMART Objectives
rubrics_metrics.description: Specific, Measurable, Achievable, Realistic, Timed.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Specific: What is being measured? Measurable: How is it being measured? Achievable: How will it be reached? Realistic: How will it be implemented? Time-Phased: When will it be completed?

rubrics_metrics.name: Program Evaluation — Before You Start (planning evaluation)
rubrics_metrics.description: Key planning questions: Why evaluate? Who needs to be involved? What information will evaluation need to provide? What key questions to answer? How will program change based on answers? Are desired measures measurable?
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Answer these before designing evaluation instruments; ensure evaluation works with program and that you can measure what you want to evaluate.

rubrics_metrics.name: Types of Evaluation
rubrics_metrics.description: Process Evaluation (who/what/how/many) and Outcome Evaluation (describing what happened; impact).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Process example: number of outreach contacts/month, cultural relevance. Outcome example: did participants increase knowledge or change behavior? Use both types appropriately and choose indicators aligned with objectives.

rubrics_metrics.name: Evaluation Methods (tools)
rubrics_metrics.description: Surveys/questionnaires (pre/post, consumer satisfaction), focus groups, program logs, interviews, case studies, post-session assessments, observational methods, and administrative recordkeeping.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Choose methods suited to questions; pilot-test instruments; ensure data entry and analysis capacity; consider literacy of participants when selecting tools (oral surveys, numbered answer sheets, observations).

rubrics_metrics.name: Focus Group Best Practices (data collection)
rubrics_metrics.description: Focus groups ideally 8–12 people with common characteristics; use skilled facilitator; ensure confidentiality; obtain consent for recordings; consider multiple focus groups until information is repetitive.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Provide respectful arrangements (refreshments, childcare, transportation, stipends), record participant selection method, background, and non-identifying demographics when reporting; include consent and confidentiality processes in budget.

rubrics_metrics.name: Key Informant & Community Interviews (data collection)
rubrics_metrics.description: Interviews (guided or unguided) identify community-specific information; key informants are leaders or gatekeepers who offer policy and norms insights.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Maintain consistency across interviews with predetermined open-ended questions; report selection process, circumstances, and non-identifying demographics; focus on recurring trends in qualitative reports.

rubrics_metrics.name: Demonstration Sessions, Observers, Games, Storytelling, Role Play (qualitative methods)
rubrics_metrics.description: Demonstration sessions are pilot runs; observers record delivery quality; games and storytelling tailor evaluation to cultural/literacy contexts; role plays/case studies assess application of learning.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Select participants like target group, use real facilitators, distribute instruments as planned; ensure adequate observers to record responses; plan games/role plays carefully to capture individual learning.

rubrics_metrics.name: Surveys — Types and Use
rubrics_metrics.description: Surveys can be self-administered or oral, collect KABB (knowledge, attitudes, beliefs, behaviors) and client satisfaction, and are often used pre/post to measure change.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Surveys are quantifiable; data entry and statistical analysis require detail-oriented staff and expertise. Use post-session assessments, pre/post-tests, or informal surveys as appropriate to literacy and sample size.

rubrics_metrics.name: Administrative Recordkeeping (evaluation/data)
rubrics_metrics.description: Consistently used record-keeping system is essential; maintain basic forms for projects; collect quantitative or qualitative info depending on usage.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Keep records current daily/monthly/quarterly/annually; design forms to match intended analytic use (e.g., monthly service logs vs. narrative reports).

rubrics_metrics.name: Developing Your Timelines
rubrics_metrics.description: Timelines should include beginning/ending dates, resources needed, persons responsible, and tasks/activities.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Ensure timelines mirror goals and objectives and are incorporated into the workplan and evaluation milestones.

rubrics_metrics.name: Developing a Budget / Budgetary Process
rubrics_metrics.description: Clearly explain all costs associated with your project; ensure figures equal requested amount and doublecheck math.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Briefly justify monetary requests in paragraph form. Budget categories include salaries, payroll taxes/benefits, fringe, consultant fees, travel, equipment, supplies, copying, telephone/fax, internet, postage, rent/utilities, evaluation costs, client incentives, indirect rate. Show revenues and expenses, including in-kind contributions and funding streams.

rubrics_metrics.name: Attachments (required documentation)
rubrics_metrics.description: Include any and all attachments the funder requests: MOU, Board list, IRS 501(c)(3) letter, resumes, job descriptions, audit or financials, sample grant if available.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Carefully follow funder-specified attachments and include them; ensure final proposals are easy to read.

rubrics_metrics.name: Interim Fiscal Policies & Procedures (internal fiscal controls)
rubrics_metrics.description: Adopt checks and balances to ensure reliability/accuracy of accounting, compliance with policies, safeguard assets, and evaluate operations.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Implement segregation of duties (at least two individuals handling transactions), authorization requirements for purchases and transactions (including higher-level approvals for Executive Director transactions), pre-numbered checks, daily deposits, monthly bank reconciliations, signatures for checks, timely investigation of returned checks, time sheet procedures, payroll tax compliance, and compliance with OMB A-122 and A-133 reporting requirements.

rubrics_metrics.name: Proposal Checklist (submission procedure)
rubrics_metrics.description: Step-by-step checklist from idea selection to post-submission follow-up.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Determine which project ideas have best chance; form planning team including clients and community leaders; design program plan; research funding sources; contact targeted funder for materials; read funder materials for instructions; prepare introduction/summary/cover letter; highlight distinguishing features; have at least one reviewer provide feedback; include requested appendices; check deadlines and number of copies; give copies to planning team; telephone the funder within two weeks after mailing the proposal.

rubrics_metrics.name: Evaluation Hip Tips (practical advice)
rubrics_metrics.description: Practical tips: have clear goals/objectives/activities; design process and outcome measures; pilot test instruments; get help with analysis if needed; be aware of audience when explaining results; you can't evaluate what you can't measure; ensure evaluation supports the program.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Pilot instruments, hire analyst if required, choose indicators aligned with objectives, and plan to use evaluation results to improve and publicize successes.
